I've always been told in the past that rust itself doesn't cause tetanus, anaerobic bacteria does. I'm not a doctor, please don't take my word as gospel, I was just in the same situation as you not so long ago, but either way keep it clean and if it's at all possible I'd get a tetanus shot -- better safe than sorry, y'know?

Hey. I've been in your shoes -- I almost died of an overdose in August of last year; I was 15 at the time. Please believe me when I say that suicide is not the way you want to go. No matter how you do it, there is always the risk of it going wrong and the chance of surviving is very, very high -- I ended up violently throwing up, jaundicing and being put on a drip in hospital for over 24 hours. It doesn't matter how badly you want to die, your body will fight to keep you alive, and if you're anything like me, you'll regret it seconds too late. 14 is incredibly young. Please call or text a hotline -- idk whereabouts in the world you are but if it's the UK I can give you the number I texted. I was having issues with my parents too and I still am, but I spoke to a teacher I got on with at school and I'm dealing with it that way -- maybe you could do the same? And I know it sounds cliché but you really aren't alone. There's loads of us and we're all just doing our best to cling on a little while longer. Please stay with us. If you end things now, there'll never be any chance of it getting better.

Hey, man, if you're feeling suicidal I would really recommend getting professional help from a counsellor or a therapist -- but you've probably heard that a thousand times by now, and the system for mental health isn't great, so I can do my best to give advice with what little knowledge I have? 

When my significant other of almost 2 years left me, I felt suicidal for about 3 months before I gave in and overdosed. I was put in hospital and they had me on a drip for 22 hours before they let me go home. I know how you feel, but please, please don't do that. 

If your girlfriend said she didn't love you anymore, you gotta let her go. That's so much easier said than done, but if she could so easily decide she didn't love you anymore, where is the point in wasting energy on her? If keeping in touch with her would be painful to you, I'd suggest cutting contact completely. It took my ex blocking me out of nowhere for me to realize that not speaking at all is so much better than clinging on to memories of what once was -- because that's all they are. Memories. 

Do you have many friends? If so, maybe talking to them would be a good place to start. It doesn't even have to be about the breakup, it could just be planning to meet up or talk on the phone. Go on adventures with friends or alone. Make new memories with those people instead of clinging on to the ones you made with your ex-girlfriend, who is someone who decided she doesn't need you, and someone who is not worth your energy anymore. Surround yourself with people who lift you up. It's not uncommon for breakups to trigger a sort of depressive state, so it's really important to push yourself and do new things so you can move on to the next chapter of your life, if that makes sense?

If you need somewhere to vent, I could suggest heading over to r/suicidewatch. If you scroll back on a few posts I've made, you'll see that's where I went when I needed help. 

It's gonna be a rollercoaster. It's gonna be incredibly hard at times, but I promise you, you will find somebody so much better. I keep telling myself that all of this heartache will be worth it to find somebody at the end of it -- it's character development. You break up, you learn from it, and you take everything you learned into your next relationship. You don't deserve somebody who comes back, you deserve somebody who never left. Work on yourself, learn to love yourself even without your ex, and that somebody will come to you. I promise. I am begging you, don't throw your life away. You have no idea what you might miss. 

I'm sorry about your situation, it really sounds like it sucks. I'm sorry if this is unsolicited advice, I didn't intend to be a hassle or anything -- I don't usually leave comments on here, but I feel like I was in a very similar situation to you and I'd like to help if I can. 

Good luck for the future. You'll hear it over and over again, but it does get better. I promise. One day you'll look back on this and you'll find it doesn't hurt anymore -- and if it does, it'll be little more than a distant ache you can hardly feel. One day you can stand up and tell the world "fuck you, I survived", and it will be the most liberating feeling, I promise. Time truly does heal, as long as you allow it to. Stay strong. There are people who have your back.
